A static website: the page is `site/index.html`, its styles are in `site/css/`, its scripts in `site/js/` and its images in `site/assets/`.

content.text:
I couldn't find anything in the site to fix, so I haven't changed any files.

- **Version history:** The repo has a single commit and a clean working tree. There is no earlier version to compare against, so I can't tell what the "last change" was.
- **Test failure:** Both screenshot tests (desktop and phone) fail, with about 1% of pixels different on desktop.
- **Layout and styling:** The page height is identical (6140px). Images, colours, sections and the nav are all in the same places.
- **What differs:** Only text rendering differs, in every heading and paragraph. In the baseline, body text is about 1px wider and headings are slightly tighter. That is just enough to re-wrap one line in the Services paragraphs ("…magni, dicta / impedit" versus "…magni, / dicta impedit").
- **Fonts:** Every font in the CSS (Roboto Slab, Montserrat, Roboto, system fonts) resolves to the locally installed Inter on this machine. The page has no `<link>` tags for Google Fonts or Font Awesome, because those lines are empty comments in `index.html`.
- **What I tried:** I tested kerning, text-rendering, optical sizing, letter-spacing, font-size, font-weight and font-family overrides against the baseline. None reduced the difference, and some made it much larger. Nothing in the CSS or HTML accounts for the change.

My best guess is that the approved screenshots were generated on a machine with a different font build or text rasterization. The site's code hasn't changed. I haven't regenerated the baselines, since that would just approve the current rendering.

I can see two ways forward:
1. If the live site looks wrong to you, tell me what you see, ideally with a screenshot or the specific section, and I'll look at that.
2. If the current look is fine, I can regenerate the baselines with `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`.

STATUS: NOT DONE
